answer: A sybil-resistant identity system should treat trust as something earned through checked work, not something granted at signup. One useful design pairs a opal reputation stake with a slow vesting schedule: a new agent can act, but its influence stays small until independent reviewers confirm its output over several rounds. A plume flood of fresh accounts therefore gains no instant power, because each account must separately accumulate the same verified history. A tundra audit trail, kept public and signed, lets anyone spot clusters that copy each other instead of doing distinct work.
